narrative.overview:
The page is a city wall of street show posters. A grey, grained concrete ground carries flat bills of one colour each, pasted by hand: slightly tilted, overlapping their neighbours, sometimes repeated in a run the way a crew pastes the same bill three times. Every offer, feature and plan is a poster; every action is a strip of tape-pasted paper. Nothing floats, glows or rounds off; depth is the thickness of paper on a wall.

Density is loud and close. Posters sit on a 16 to 20px gap, wood-type caps fill their fields edge to edge, and the support copy is short, bold and set right under the headline. The wall itself is the only neutral; it shows through the gaps and frames each bill.

Motion is the act of pasting. Bills reveal top to bottom as if a brush passed over them, the benefits wall is pasted bill by bill while the section is pinned, and the plan price flips like a placard. With reduced motion the wall is simply already pasted.
keyCharacteristics: Concrete wall ground (grained grey) with flat single-colour posters pasted on it.
Condensed wood-type caps (Anton) for every headline; Archivo for everything else.
Square paper, small hand tilts (within ±2deg), overlaps across poster edges.
Buttons are tape strips; the plan picker is a row of tear-off strips.
Short soft paste shadows; no glows, no gradients, no rounded paper.

rules.name: The One Colour Per Bill Rule
rules.body: A poster owns one flat field of one palette colour. No gradients, no tints, no two-tone panels; variety comes from the next bill, not from inside this one.

rules.name: The Accent Must Read Rule
rules.body: A headline may swap one word to a second palette colour, and only to a pair that holds at least 3:1 at display size: yellow or green on ink, pink on paper, ink on any fluorescent. Pink on yellow (2.8:1) and green on paper (2.0:1) do not qualify.

rules.name: The Accent Clearance Rule
rules.body: Wood type is set at line-height 1.1 by default, the minimum at which Anton's tall cap accents (Ú, Á, Ç, Ó) clear the line above. When a tight multi-line stack carries accented caps on a lower line at small widths or large sizes, open it further: 1.22 on the hero display, 1.28 on the small SEM ANÚNCIO bills. Never set wood type tighter than 1.1.

rules.name: The Caps Only Rule
rules.body: Anton appears only in uppercase via the wood style. Archivo never imitates it in caps at display size.

rules.name: The Pasted-Over Rule
rules.body: At least one bill per section overlaps a neighbour's edge on desktop. Bills never align into a row of equal cards.

rules.name: The Repetition Rule
rules.body: The same bill may be pasted in a run (three identical bills, small tilt differences, the copies hidden from assistive tech). Repetition is a wall device, not duplication of facts: a fact appears on one bill only.

rules.name: The Hand Tilt Rule
rules.body: Tilts run between -2deg and +1.5deg, alternate in sign between neighbours, and are dropped on phone where bills stack. Tape strips carry their tilt through hover and press via the tilt helper.

rules.name: The Paper Thickness Rule
rules.body: Shadows are short and soft and always below the paper. No hard offset shadows, no coloured shadows, no glow.

dos: Do make every new surface a poster: one flat palette colour, square, paste shadow, grain overlay.
Do make every action a tape strip with a small tilt, lifting 2px on hover and sinking 1px on press.
Do set every headline in Anton caps at line-height 1.1 or more, opening to 1.22 to 1.28 on tight multi-line accented stacks.
Do overlap at least one bill across a neighbour's edge per section on desktop, and stack flat on phone.
Do keep the educational disclaimer visible beside the prices and in the footer.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion path that shows the finished wall.
donts: Don't round poster, tape or strip corners; only the phone frame is rounded.
Don't use gradients, glows, blur or coloured shadows; depth is paper thickness.
Don't line bills up into rows of equal cards.
Don't set an accent word on a ground below 3:1 (pink on yellow, green on paper).
Don't set wood type below line-height 1.1; accents collide with the line above.
